question: In 2019, _______ was appointed as Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Walmart.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Suresh Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Suresh Kumar** was appointed as the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Walmart in 2019.
 
• Before joining Walmart, he held leadership roles at Google and Amazon.
 
• At Google, he served as the vice president and general manager of display, video, app ads, and analytics.
 
• He also served as the vice president of technology at Amazon, where he led initiatives in retail, marketplace systems, and infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Technology Officer (CTO)**

 
 
• The CTO is responsible for overseeing the development and dissemination of technology for external customers, vendors, and other clients to help improve and increase business.
 
• They are pivotal in deciding the company's technology strategy and ensuring the technological resources align with the business needs.
 
 
 
• **Walmart**
 
 
• Walmart Inc. is an American multinational retail corporation that operates a chain of hypermarkets, discount department stores, and grocery stores.
 
• Founded by Sam Walton in 1962, Walmart is headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas.
 
• As of 2021, Walmart is the world's largest company by revenue, with approximately $559 billion in annual revenue.
 
 
 
• **Google**
 
 
• Google LLC is an American multinational technology company that specializes in Internet-related services and products.
 
• These include online advertising technologies, a search engine, cloud computing, software, and hardware.
 
 
 
• **Amazon**
 
 
• Amazon.com, Inc. is an American multinational technology company which focuses on e-commerce, cloud computing, digital streaming, and artificial intelligence.
 
• It is considered one of the Big Five companies in the U.S. information technology industry, along with Google, Apple, Microsoft, and Facebook.
